## phenix settings db

View or edit legacy database settings

### Synopsis

```text
Manage legacy settings stored in the internal database. For active runtime configuration (logging, etc.), use the root settings commands (get/set).
```

```text
phenix settings db [flags]
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help   help for db
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix settings](settings.md) - View, list, or edit phenix system settings
* [phenix settings db edit](settings.md#phenix-settings-db-edit) - Edit a setting in the database
* [phenix settings db list](settings.md#phenix-settings-db-list) - List settings in the database

## phenix settings db edit

Edit a setting in the database

### Synopsis

```text
Edit a setting in the database. This command does not change the log settings: use 'phenix settings set' for them (for example, phenix settings set log.system.max-size 100).
```

```text
phenix settings db edit <category> <name> <value> [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix settings db edit <category> <name> <newValue>
phenix settings db edit Password MinLength 20
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help   help for edit
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix settings db](settings.md#phenix-settings-db) - View or edit legacy database settings

## phenix settings get

Get configuration value(s)

### Synopsis

```text
Gets a configuration value from the runtime configuration. If no key is provided, returns all settings.
```

```text
phenix settings get [key] [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix settings get
phenix settings get log.level
phenix settings get log -o json
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help            help for get
      --json            Output as JSON (the same as -o json)
  -o, --output string   Output format (table, json, yaml) (default "yaml")
```

## phenix settings set

Set a configuration value

### Synopsis

```text
Sets a configuration value in the YAML config file phenix read, or, when it read none, in $HOME/.config/phenix/config.yaml (/etc/phenix/config.yaml as root), creating it. A flag or PHENIX_ environment variable for the key still overrides the file. The value of a phenix setting must have the type of its flag, such as an integer for log.system.max-size; a string setting keeps the text as it is. For other keys, true or false becomes a boolean and a number becomes a number. Comments and the other keys in the file stay.
```

```text
phenix settings set <key> <value> [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix settings set log.level debug
phenix settings set log.system.max-size 200
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help   help for set
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix settings](settings.md) - View, list, or edit phenix system settings

## phenix settings unset

Unset configuration value(s)

### Synopsis

```text
Unsets a configuration value in the config file phenix read, so a PHENIX_ environment variable or the default applies. Comments and the other keys in the file stay. A key that is not in the file does not change the file. Use --all to reset all settings. With --dry-run, phenix shows the key that it would remove, or the config file that it would delete, and changes nothing.
```

```text
phenix settings unset [key] [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix settings unset log.level
phenix settings unset log.level --dry-run
phenix settings unset --all
```

### Options

```text
      --all       Unset all settings (delete configuration file)
      --dry-run   Show what the command would change, and change nothing
  -h, --help      help for unset
```
